rumours: Ash came down on Raven Rock again last night. The Redoran Guard swept the Bulwark at dawn, and still my bread tastes of Red Mountain.
The Skaal won't sell stalhrim to anyone. A Telvanni offered them a chest of drakes for one sliver, and they laughed him all the way back to his mushroom.
Folk wake up with raw hands and stone dust in their hair and no memory of the night. My cousin found her boots full of ash. People whisper about the Earth Stone.
Rieklings came down to the road past Thirsk Mead Hall with spears and a stolen war-horn. Little blue things, but there were twenty of them, and they were laughing.
Somebody at Tel Mithryn pays good coin for Dwemer scrap out of Kagrumez. Telvanni coin, mind. Count it twice and bite every piece.
Fort Frostmoth's been empty since the Red Year. Empty of the living, anyway. Fishermen won't beach on that shore after dark.
Reavers have dug in at Bujold's Retreat. Wreckers and cutthroats from every port between Windhelm and Necrom, and the Skaal say they've started taking their sledges.
legends: The Skaal say the frost giant Karstaag once ruled the north of the island from a hall of living ice. When he fell, his blood froze into the walls, and that is why the ice of Castle Karstaag never melts, even in Sun's Height.

In the last age the moon over Solstheim turned red, and the Huntsman of the Princes came down to play his game with mortal prey. The beasts of the island still remember. When the moon swells, the wolves that are not wolves gather at Frostmoon Crag.

Stalhrim is ice the All-Maker made to remember. A smith who works it without a prayer will find the blade cold to the bone and the edge turning on its master. Only the Skaal know the words, and they do not teach them to strangers.

Haknir Death-Brand sailed the Sea of Ghosts with a crew sworn to follow him past dying. His ship broke on the shoal that bears his name. On still nights you can hear oars dip where no boat floats, and a voice counting the stroke.

songs.title: Ash from the South
lines: Ash from the south and ice from the north,
The island between them holds its breath.
Raven on the wall and Skaal by the fire,
Each keeps a watch, and each keeps death.
Sing to the stones when the night walks loud,
And do not answer the one in the cloud.

songs.title: The Riekling's Horn
lines: Small blue thief with a horn too big,
Rides on a boar and dances a jig,
Stole the mead of Thirsk and the bench beside,
Now the Nords drink snow and the rieklings ride.

raven_rock.hook: The Dunmer town of Raven Rock squats behind the Bulwark, its roofs grey with ash from Red Mountain. The Redoran Guard keeps the wall, the mine keeps the coin, and lately the townsfolk keep waking up far from their beds.
raven_rock.rumour: The Guard doubled the watch on the Bulwark. Not for ash spawn this time. For our own people, walking out of the gate in their sleep with their eyes wide open.

notes.title: Standing Orders for the Bulwark Watch
notes.author: Mileth Indaram, Sergeant of the Redoran Guard
pages:
^By leave of the Councilor
1. The south gate is barred from dusk to first light. No exceptions for Company men, Telvanni errand-boys, or anyone who claims to have forgotten their pipe at the Retching Netch.
2. Any citizen seen walking toward the Earth Stone at night is to be stopped, gently. Do not wake them by shouting. Turn them by the shoulders and walk them home.

3. Ash spawn are to be fought at the wall, never past it. Last Seed taught us that lesson at the cost of two good guards.
4. Grave-diggers bound for Kolbjorn Barrow carry a pass with my seal. If they come back without the pass, they come back without their wages.
5. Report anything strange. I am aware that this is Solstheim and everything is strange. Report it anyway.

notes.title: Letter to the Grey Quarter
notes.author: Ilvi Sadrano
pages:
Brother,
You asked whether Raven Rock is better than Windhelm. The Nords here do not spit at us. The ash, on the other hand, gets into everything: the bedding, the scuttle, my teeth. I sweep the step four times a day and Mother says it is the ancestors visiting.

Something else, and do not laugh. Three nights ago I woke on the road outside the gate with my hands bleeding and a stone in each fist. Old Aulus, the Imperial, found me and walked me back. He says he saw a dozen others out there, all carrying stones toward the west. Nobody remembers. Nobody wants to talk about it. Send word from Windhelm if you hear of a cure for walking in one's sleep. Your sister, Ilvi.

skaal_village.hook: A ring of timber longhouses in the northern snows, home of the Skaal, who honour the All-Maker and trust no one who comes asking for stalhrim. Their hunters know every trail of the island.
skaal_village.rumour: The Skaal let me trade furs once. They looked at my iron knife like it was a sickness. Their hunter Yrsa says reavers have been raiding their sledges near Bujold's Retreat.

notes.title: Yrsa's Tally Stick, Read Aloud
notes.author: Yrsa Seal-Singer
pages:
#Notches since the first frost
Six horker at Horker Island. Thanks given for each, fat kept, bones returned to the water.
Two bristlebacks near Bristleback Cave. One too young, let go.
One bear. It gave itself on the third day, as bears do.

Two sledges lost on the shore road south of Gyldenhul Barrow. Not lost. Taken. Iron-shod boot tracks, smell of tar and cheap mead. Reavers from Bujold's Retreat. They took Old Skjald's carved hunting-mask, which was his father's, and his father's. The Adversary is in men who take what they did not make.

notes.title: Words Before the Hunt
pages:
~All-Maker, you made the snow and the seal beneath it.
~You made the spear-arm and the hunger.
~What I take today I do not own;
~I hold it for a while, as I hold my breath.
~When I fall, take me back the way you take the beast:
~without anger, and without waste.

Spoken by every Skaal hunter at the edge of the village before the hunt, with the right hand on the doorpost and the left on the spear. Children learn it before they learn to throw. Outlanders who hear it sometimes laugh. The Skaal let them laugh, and notice which ones come home from the ice with full sledges and which do not.

thirsk_mead_hall.hook: A great Nord mead hall on the island's eastern slopes, raised in the last age and fought over ever since. The hall has been won back from the rieklings, but its heirloom spear has not.
thirsk_mead_hall.rumour: They say the Nords at Thirsk took the hall back from the rieklings last winter. Took the hall, not the spear. The riekling chief at Frossel still carries it, and Brenna Ice-Mead won't sleep until it's home.

notes.title: Carvings on the Mead Hall Beam
pages:
^Here the chieftains of Thirsk are named
The first carved the beam. The second set the hearth. The third went hunting the great bristleback alone and came back with half a hand and the whole beast.

Below the names, in fresher cuts: The hall fell to the small blue folk in the winter of the black ice. Their chief carried off the Spear of Thirsk, and they danced in our benches and drank our honey. We took it back with axes. The spear is still in Frossel. The beam has room for the name of whoever brings it home.

notes.title: Brenna's Letter to Raven Rock
notes.author: Brenna Ice-Mead
pages:
To Geldis Sadri at the Retching Netch,
You owe me for four casks of honey-mead, and I owe you an apology for the state of your back room after my cousins drank there. Call it even. I need a favour instead of coin.

Send me anyone who can fight and does not drink more than they kill. The riekling chief who calls himself Kruk Gnaw-Tooth sits at Frossel on the north shore with the Spear of Thirsk across his knees. My people will not follow me into that den again until someone shows them it can be done. I will pay what I have, and the spear goes to the one who takes it, if they swear to bring it to the hall on feast days. Brenna.

tel_mithryn.hook: A Telvanni tower grown from a giant mushroom on the island's southeastern coast. The wizard Neloth rules here, and his household of nervous apprentices pays well for anything Dwemer, dangerous, or both.
tel_mithryn.rumour: Tel Mithryn? The scholar Ulvo Nerano will pay you for Dwemer rubbish, so long as you don't touch anything on the way in. Last fellow who touched something grew a second shadow.

notes.title: Survey of the Island's Dwemer Sites
notes.author: Ulvo Nerano, scholar of Tel Mithryn
pages:
A provisional list, compiled at my own expense since the master considers the subject beneath him.
I. Nchardak, to the east. Flooded, partly. The master has opinions about it which he shares at length and in no useful detail.
II. Kagrumez, west of the dragon mound. The resonance chambers still hum. The gems sing; I wish to know in what key.

III. Fahlbtharz, far to the north and west, where the steam pipes have not stopped hissing in four thousand years. A prospector from the Company went in last spring. He came out with burns on both arms and a theory, neither of which he would explain.
Note to self: hire someone sturdier than myself. Possibly several someones.

notes.title: Notice to Visitors of Tel Mithryn
notes.author: Steward of the tower
pages:
Visitors to the tower are reminded:
Do not touch the netches. They are not pets.
Do not touch the apprentices. They are not pets either, though some of them may be experiments.
Do not ask the master about his age, his health, his rivals, or Vvardenfell.
Do not climb the stalks. The levitation stops working at the top for anyone the master has not keyed into it. He has keyed in no one.
The steward accepts no responsibility for growths, curses, or transfigurations acquired while ignoring this notice.

old_attius_farm.hook: An old homestead south of Raven Rock, where hardy ash-yams grow in volcanic dirt. The farmer here has been short of help since his son took work digging at Kolbjorn Barrow.
old_attius_farm.rumour: Tilvur Sadas grows the only decent yams on the island. His boy went digging for that excavator Ralis Sedarys at Kolbjorn Barrow. Hasn't come home for supper in a week.

notes.title: Old Attius Farm Accounts
notes.author: Tilvur Sadas
pages:
#Hearthfire, 4E 201
Ash-yams, eleven baskets to the Retching Netch: 33 drakes.
Scathecraw, one bundle to the apothecary: 8 drakes.
New hoe blade from the smith: owed, 12 drakes.
Neral's first wages from the diggers at Kolbjorn Barrow: 20 drakes. Good boy.

#Frostfall
Ash-yams, six baskets. The ash blight took the north rows.
Neral's wages: none. The foreman says they will be paid when the dig reaches the inner door.
Neral's wages: none.
Neral has not come home. I have written to the Guard. I will go up to the barrow myself if the sergeant does nothing. A farmer with a hoe is better than no one.

glacial_cave.hook: A cave of blue ice in the far north, veined with stalhrim. The Skaal cut it with prayers and patience. The men who took the cave this winter cut it with neither.
glacial_cave.rumour: Aevar Stone-Ear, the Skaal smith, sent his apprentice to the Glacial Cave to cut stalhrim the proper way. Boy found smugglers there instead, and the ice spirits are angry.

notes.title: Stalhrim Cutting Tally
notes.author: Torvar Half-Ear
pages:
Slabs cut: 14. Slabs cracked in the cutting: 9. The stuff fights the chisel like it's alive.
Buyer in Windhelm pays 300 a slab if it reaches him whole. The Skaal boy we caught says it never reaches anyone whole without the words. I said he can teach us the words or he can stay tied up. He's chosen to stay tied up. Stubborn little seal.

Something walks in the deep ice now. White, see-through, cold enough to stop your heart from across the cave. Bjorn says it's a wraith, come because we cut without asking. Bjorn also says we should let the boy go. Bjorn's getting a smaller share.

notes.title: Words Scratched in the Ice
notes.author: Hjalmar, apprentice of Aevar
pages: Hjalmar was here. Tied three days. They took the cutting pick my master gave me; it has his mark on the haft, a hand and a hammer. If I do not come back, whoever reads this, take the pick to Aevar Stone-Ear in the Skaal Village. Tell him I did not teach them the words. Tell him the ice is crying.

Lower down, smaller, as if written later by a colder hand: They argue at night about the words. Torvar says there are no words, only Skaal tricks. Bjorn is not so sure. The white thing in the deep ice came closer tonight. It stood over me and did not touch me. I think it knows who taught me.

castle_karstaag_ruins.hook: The ice-bound ruin of the frost giant Karstaag's hall, slain in the last age. Something has taken up his throne, and the cold coming off it can be felt from Mortrag Peak.
castle_karstaag_ruins.rumour: The giant Karstaag died two hundred years ago, they say. So why are there giant tracks in the snow outside his castle, big as a cart and fresh as this morning?

notes.title: Journal of a Frozen Hunter
notes.author: Eirik Snow-Born
pages:
#14th of Evening Star
Camped below Mortrag Peak. The old Skaal story says Karstaag's bones lie in the castle with a crown of ice still on his skull. A crown of ice that never melts is worth a fortune to the right mage in Tel Mithryn.

#16th of Evening Star
The bones are not here. Something larger than a man dragged them deeper, and there are fresh tracks: wide, three-toed, with frost blooming in every print. Not Karstaag. His get, maybe. The Skaal say giants of the ice have long memories and longer children.

#17th
It sat on the old throne and watched me. It did not attack. I think it wanted me to leave something. My fingers do not work any more. Whoever finds this: the crown shard is in its fist.

notes.title: Skaal Marker Stone
pages:
Carved in the Skaal manner, with a frost-giant's hand cut beneath the words:
This was the hall of the cold king. He fell. His blood did not. Do not bring fire here, for the ice remembers burning. Do not take, for the ice remembers taking. Whoever sits the cold throne now is no friend to the All-Maker's children.

Beneath the giant hand, a second carving, newer and shallower: Eirik Snow-Born went past this stone in Evening Star seeking the crown of ice. We told him the crown is not a thing to be sold. He said everything is a thing to be sold. The stone is still here. Eirik is not.

frossel.hook: A riekling den in a sea cave on the north shore, stinking of horker fat and stolen mead. Its chief carries a spear that once hung in Thirsk Mead Hall.
frossel.rumour: Frossel is where the rieklings go to sleep off our mead. Their chief has a spear twice as long as he is and a temper twice as long as that.

notes.title: Charcoal Pictures on a Horker Hide
pages: A rough set of drawings, described here by whoever found them: a small blue figure holding a very long spear above its head. Many small figures bowing. A large hairy figure, clearly a Nord, lying flat with crosses for eyes. A mead barrel drawn with great love and detail. Last, the long spear stuck into the ground beside a fire, with the small figure asleep against it, and a horker standing guard. The horker has been given a crown.
On the back of the hide, someone from Thirsk has added in charcoal: The big hairy figure is Gunnar, I think. He is not dead. He will be annoyed to see this.

notes.title: Hunter's Notes on Frossel
notes.author: Gunnar of Thirsk
pages: Watched Frossel for two days from the rocks above Haknir's Shoal. Count: twenty rieklings, more when the boats come back. Two bristlebacks that they ride. One chief, Kruk Gnaw-Tooth, who carries the Spear of Thirsk and never puts it down, not even to eat.

They are not stupid. They post a watcher on the cliff and change him at dusk. They are afraid of fire and of loud singing, which we discovered by accident. Tell Brenna: go at dusk, go loud, and go with more than three. I went with three. I am the only one writing.

saerings_watch.hook: A high stone perch in the snowy north where a dragon once kept watch for the Dragon Priests. Wingbeats echo off the peaks again, and the old word wall is scorched black.
saerings_watch.rumour: A dragon roosts on Saering's Watch. I've seen it circle Frykte Peak at dawn. The Skaal say it's waiting for someone. I don't intend to find out who.

notes.title: The Watch of Saering
pages:
~Saering sat on the high grey rock,
~Watching the sea for the tall ships' mast,
~Watching the snow for the hunters' track,
~Watching the priests till the priests had passed.

~The priests are bones, the ships are wood,
~The hunters' grandsons hunt no more,
~But Saering's children keep the watch,
~And still they count us, shore to shore.

~Old Saering sleeps, his children wake,
~They wheel above the Frykte stone.
~Who climbs the watch must bring a voice,
~Or climb the watch and stay alone.
The Skaal sing this to children who wander too far north. Then they sing it again, slower, to the ones who wander back.

notes.title: Burned Log of a Dragon Hunter
notes.author: Ragnvald the Patient
pages:
#3rd of Sun's Dusk
Set up the ballista bolts on the ridge. The beast comes back to the watch every dusk and lands beside the word wall. It speaks to the wall. I swear it. It speaks, and the letters glow.

#5th of Sun's Dusk
We hit it once. Once. Halla is burned. Ofeig ran. I am writing this behind the word wall, which the fire does not seem to touch. If you find this, do not come with three men and a bolt-thrower. Come with a Voice, or do not come at all.

bristleback_cave.hook: A cave in the northwestern hills where the island's bristlebacks den through the worst of the winter. A trapper made it his larder; the boars have made him part of theirs.
bristleback_cave.rumour: Bristleback Cave? Old Rolf Hide-Seller set his snares there every winter. Third winter running he came back with a full sledge. This winter the sledge came back alone.

notes.title: Trapper's Snare Log
notes.author: Rolf Hide-Seller
pages:
#Sun's Dusk
Snares set along the gully, twelve of them. Two bristlebacks taken, good hides, bad tempers. Sold the tusks to the miners at Broken Tusk Mine, who think it is funny to hang them over their door. Funny until the rieklings came for the tusks too.

#Evening Star
Something has been at the snares before me. Not a boar. Not a bear. It ate the bait, the boar, and the snare, and left the stake chewed to splinters. I am going deeper to see what it is. The hides are worth it. The hides are always worth it, until they aren't.

notes.title: Plank Nailed at the Cave Mouth
pages: Painted in red ochre by some passing hunter: SOWS WITH YOUNG INSIDE. They will not run. They will not stop. If you hear grunting, you are already too close. Rolf's sledge is at the bottom of the gully if anyone wants it. Rolf does not.

Underneath, in charcoal, a second hand: Rolf went in on the twelfth of Evening Star with a torch and a boar-spear and his best hides on his back. He always said the hides were worth it. If you find a fur pack with a red thong on it, it was his. Leave it. The sows have made a nest of it.

frykte_peak.hook: A wind-scoured summit beside Saering's Watch, named by the Skaal for fear. From its top you can see the whole frozen north, and the dragon that circles it.
frykte_peak.rumour: Frykte means fear in the old Skaal tongue. My grandfather said they named it after the first man who climbed it and saw what was sitting on the next peak over.

notes.title: Note Weighted in a Summit Cairn
pages: Climbed in two days from the Headwaters of Harstrad. Built this cairn on the third. On a clear morning I counted: the ice of Castle Karstaag, the tusks of the Broken Tusk hills, the black barrow of Benkongerike, and the sea beyond Haknir's Shoal. And on the next rock, so close I could see the scales, a dragon asleep on Saering's Watch. I did not finish my count. Add a stone if you came up here and lived. There are four stones.

haknirs_shoal.hook: The rotting wreck of Haknir Death-Brand's ship, caught on the rocks of the north shore. His crew swore to sail with him past death, and the tide has never quite let them stop rowing.
haknirs_shoal.rumour: Haknir's Shoal. Don't go there at night. I mean it. My father heard the oars once, and a voice calling the stroke, and there was no boat on the water at all.

notes.title: Articles of the Death-Brand's Crew
notes.author: Haknir Death-Brand
pages:
^Sworn on the brand-iron
Every man who signs below shares the take in eight parts: two to the captain, one to the mate, one to the brand-iron's keeping, four among the oars.
No man leaves the oar while the captain lives. No man leaves the oar when the captain dies. The brand-iron keeps the oath, and the oath keeps the oars.

Thirty-one marks follow, some names, some only crosses. At the bottom, in a different hand, scrawled later: The iron is still in the captain's chest. As long as it is there, they row. Somebody take it out and throw it in a fire. Please.

notes.title: Salvager's Scratched Board
notes.author: Sigrid Net-Mender
pages: I took the purser's coin from the Death-Brand's hold before the oarsmen woke. Too heavy to swim back with. Buried it on Horker Island, east of the barrow, under the flat stone the old bull horker sleeps on, about twenty paces north of the island's middle. If the bull is still there, wait for him to go fishing. He always goes fishing at noon. I will come back for it in spring. If I do not, it was never mine anyway.

mortrag_peak.hook: A crown of rock and glacier in the north, above Castle Karstaag. In the last age the Huntsman's prey was hunted across this ice, and the hunters say the ice has not forgotten.
mortrag_peak.rumour: Mortrag Peak is where it all ended the year the moon went red. The old Skaal won't say what happened. They'll only say the glacier ate a lot of hunters.

notes.title: What the Glacier Kept
notes.author: Skjald the Elder, as told to a Raven Rock scribe
pages: In my grandmother's grandmother's time the moon bled and a great hunt was called across Solstheim. The prey was a mortal, and the hunters were not. They raced across this glacier and down into the halls beneath it, and where they fought the ice cracked, and where it cracked it swallowed.

We still find them sometimes, when the summer is long. A hand in the ice. A spear. Once a wolf with a man's eyes, frozen in mid-leap. We leave them where they are. The All-Maker gave the ice to keep them, and who are we to open a gift that was not given to us?

benkongerike.hook: A Nordic barrow sunk into the snow north of the Headwaters of Harstrad. The Skaal call it the House That Coughs, for the wind that blows out of its door, and they will not camp in its sight.
benkongerike.rumour: Benkongerike? A Thirsk skald went in there last moon to sing the dead to sleep. Said they deserved a song. The dead didn't agree, apparently.

notes.title: Unfinished Verses of Orm the Skald
notes.author: Orm of Thirsk
pages:
~Sleep, old jarls, in your house of stone,
~The ships are burnt and the songs are gone.
~I bring you one, a little late:
~Lie down, lie down, and shut the gate.

Orm's hand, on the back, much shakier: They do not want lullabies. They want the names of the men who buried them, and I do not know the names. The one in the iron crown keeps asking. I have started making names up. He knows.

The last lines are barely legible: He has stopped asking. He has started singing. He has a better voice than I do, which is the cruellest thing of all. If any Thirsk folk find this, tell Brenna I owed her for two casks, and tell her I am sorry.

notes.title: Rubbing from the Inner Door
notes.author: Ulvo Nerano
pages: A partial rubbing, taken in charcoal and much smudged. The script is old Nordic, cruder than mainland work. My reading: Here lie the sworn of the first landing, who came over the ice from Skyrim and found the island already spoken for. The rest, I think, lists who spoke for it and how many they had to kill. The door below is cut with a dragon's head, its mouth sealed with iron. I did not try the door. I have more sense than skalds.

broken_tusk_mine.hook: A Nord mine in the northwestern hills, named for the bristleback tusk nailed over its entrance. The miners fled when the rieklings came for the tusk, and stayed fled when the rieklings stayed.
broken_tusk_mine.rumour: Broken Tusk Mine paid well until the rieklings moved in. Foreman Hrefna says they've built a throne out of ore carts. She wants it back. The mine, not the throne.

notes.title: Broken Tusk Mine Ledger
notes.author: Hrefna, foreman
pages:
#Frostfall
Iron, 40 measures. Silver, 6. One seam of black ice at the bottom gallery, which the Skaal say is stalhrim and is not ours to cut. Left it alone. Wages paid in full.
#Sun's Dusk
Iron, 22 measures. Rieklings seen on the ridge three times. Posted a watch.

#Evening Star
Rieklings in the bottom gallery. Fifteen at least. They came up through a crack we did not know was there. Torvi lost a finger. We ran. The claim stone with the Jarl's seal is still in the strongbox in the bottom gallery, and without it the Company will say the mine is anyone's. Whoever brings it back gets a share of the first year's iron.

notes.title: Rieklings' Tally Marks on a Cart
pages: Scratched into the side of an ore cart, with pictures where the rieklings did not know the letters: Tusk, one (picture of tusk, very proud). Boots, four. Mead, none, angry face. Pick, six. Nord, zero, then crossed out and made into one, then crossed out again and made into zero. Pictures of the chief sitting on the cart and the other rieklings pushing. It appears to be a list of the mine's riches as the new owners understand them.

At the very bottom, beside a picture of a horker with a crown, someone has added a single Nordic word in a neat miner's hand: Hrefna. Whether it was the foreman herself, insulted at being left off, nobody has asked.

stalhrim_source.hook: A seam of stalhrim, the deathless blue ice of Solstheim, breaking the surface of the snowfield. The Skaal guard its secret; smugglers guard their caches nearby.
stalhrim_source.rumour: There's a place where the black ice comes right up out of the snow, below Mortrag Peak. Smugglers bury what they cut and come back for it in spring. Most of them come back.

notes.title: Words Cut Beside the Ice
pages: In the Skaal runes, with a hand pressed flat beneath them: This ice is the All-Maker's memory. Cut it with thanks, and it will cut for you. Cut it with greed, and it will remember you. We have cut here for a hundred winters and taken only what we needed. The ice keeps count. The ice keeps count of you too, stranger.

Lower, in the trade-tongue of Raven Rock, scratched in by somebody else entirely: We tried. Three of us, one winter. Two came home. The one who did not come home was the one who laughed at this stone. I am writing this here so that the next one who laughs reads it first.

headwaters_of_harstrad.hook: A clearing where hot springs bubble up through the snow and feed the river Harstrad. Hunters come to warm their bones; so do the beasts that hunt the hunters.
headwaters_of_harstrad.rumour: The Headwaters are the only warm place north of Thirsk. Lovely for a soak. Keep your spear near the bank, though: the bears think so too.

notes.title: Initials Carved in a Pine
pages: Two sets of initials cut deep into the bark, H and S, inside a heart that someone has tried to make look like a horker. Below, newer: S came here every Midyear for ten years. This Midyear H came alone. She sat in the warm water and sang his song, and a bear sat on the far bank and listened, and neither bothered the other. Some things the All-Maker allows.

Lower still, in a child's careful letters: My grandmother is S. She says H. still comes to the water in her dreams, and that the bear is still listening. She says if I ever marry, I must bring my husband here first and make him sing. I do not think I will marry. The water is too warm to leave.

white_ridge_barrow.hook: A Nordic tomb cut into the white ridge below Mortrag Peak. Its draugr wear stalhrim at their throats, and a smuggler's map says not all of their ice stayed buried.
white_ridge_barrow.rumour: White Ridge Barrow. The smugglers who cut stalhrim out there used it as a hiding hole. Then something in the deep rooms started taking its share.

notes.title: Smuggler's Map Scrap
notes.author: Bjorn Cold-Hands
pages: Torvar thinks the stash is in the barrow. It was, until the dead started moving. I moved it. Stalhrim Source, west of the black ice, eleven paces past the split rock, under the slab with the Skaal hand cut into it. Ha. Let them blame the Skaal. If you are reading this, Torvar, I took my share and then some. If you are not Torvar, take it with my blessing; it is better than him having it.

Scrawled on the back in charcoal: Torvar, if you are reading the back too, you are even more of a fool than I thought. Do not go to the Glacial Cave again. The ice there is waking. I am done with ice. I am going to Windhelm to sell fish.

notes.title: Epitaph in the Burial Hall
pages: Cut above a row of niches, each holding a body wrapped in furs gone stiff with frost: Here lie the ice-wardens of the white ridge. They kept the black ice from the hands of greed, and were buried with a sliver at their throats, that they might keep it still. Waken them only if you have come to give, not take. The wardens do not know the difference between a smuggler and a pilgrim. They have stopped caring.
Someone has scratched beneath it, in a hurry: Five of the niches are empty now. The slivers were taken from their throats. We should not have taken the slivers.

hrothmunds_barrow.hook: An ancient tomb in the snowy uplands, where masked strangers have been seen carrying lanterns down the steps. The Skaal say Hrothmund was a traitor once. Someone is praying to traitors again.
hrothmunds_barrow.rumour: Masked folk going in and out of Hrothmund's Barrow. Not draugr. People. They wear the same masks as those cultists who attacked travellers at the docks. Nobody's been brave enough to ask what they want.

notes.title: Devotion of the Faithful
notes.author: Ulfgar Ash-Mask
pages:
~The first was taken, the first was wronged,
~The first will wake and take what is his.
~We dig in his name and sleep in his dream,
~We open the doors the traitors sealed.

Beneath, in plain prose: Hrothmund betrayed the Master in the old days and was buried with the key to a door the Master once used. Brother Ulfgar will find the key. The sleepers from Raven Rock will carry the stones. When the key is found, the Master will remember who opened the door, and the ones who did not will build his halls forever.

notes.title: The Turncoat Hrothmund
notes.author: Storn's apprentice
pages: Hrothmund served the dragon-masked priests in the old days, when the island was theirs. When the people rose against the priests he took a torch and burned the doors of his own master's house. Some called him a hero. The priests called him a thief. He was buried here under a stone with no name, and with him a key no one could explain. The Skaal do not go here. Not because he was a traitor, but because a man who betrays once is buried uneasily.

gyldenhul_barrow.hook: A Nordic tomb on the eastern shore, a short walk from the Skaal village. Young Skaal hunters once went down its stairs to prove themselves. Lately they go down and do not come back up.
gyldenhul_barrow.rumour: Brandr, Yrsa's nephew, went into Gyldenhul Barrow to prove he was a man. The Skaal don't make their boys do that any more. He did it anyway.

notes.title: Brandr's Note to His Aunt
notes.author: Brandr
pages:
Aunt Yrsa,
You said the old proving was done with. You said nobody has to walk into Gyldenhul any more. But the old men still talk about who went in and who came back, and they never talk about me. I am taking Father's spear. The one with the seal-tooth on the shaft.

If I come back you can be angry at me. If I do not come back, do not send anyone after me who does not want to go. I mean that. The All-Maker gives and takes, and I would rather be taken than be nothing. Brandr.

notes.title: Proving Marks on the Stair
pages: On the wall of the stair, generations of Skaal marks: a hand, a spear, a name, cut by the young hunters who came down and walked out again. The oldest are worn almost smooth. The newest is a single spear-mark with a seal tooth drawn beside it and no name yet, as if the carver meant to finish it on the way out. Further down the stair the marks stop. Something has scraped the wall clean.

Below the last marks, at the turn of the stair, a crude warning has been chalked by some Skaal elder: The proving is ended. Go home. If you will not go home, go with two companions and a torch, and come back by dusk, or your mother will cut your name on this wall herself.

horker_island.hook: A rocky islet east of Gyldenhul Barrow where horkers haul out by the hundred. The Skaal hunt here with thanks; a salvager buried a purse here with none.
horker_island.rumour: Horker Island stinks worse than a Windhelm tannery. There's a bull horker there the size of a longboat that the Skaal won't hunt. They say he's lucky.

notes.title: Hunting Stone of Horker Island
pages: Cut in Skaal runes on a stone above the tide line: Take one in ten. Take none with calves. Do not take the old bull, who has fathered half the island and is the All-Maker's own joke. Return the bones to the water before you sail. Leave no fire burning. Leave no blood unwashed. The horkers remember, and so do we.

Scratched underneath, in Cyrodilic, by a less respectful visitor: The old bull bit my boat. I have never in my life been so insulted by an animal. He is still there, by the flat stone in the middle of the island. Do not take him. He is not worth it. He is entirely made of spite.

snowclad_ruins.hook: Broken Nordic stones half-buried in snow above the Moesring Pass, crowned by a word wall that hums when the wind blows from the north. Scholars come here. Some stay longer than they meant to.
snowclad_ruins.rumour: There's writing on the old wall at Snowclad Ruins that only dragons can read. A scholar from the mainland sat in front of it for a week trying. Got frostbite and a headache for his trouble.

notes.title: Letter from a Frostbitten Scholar
notes.author: Aurelian Brightquill, of the Synod
pages:
Esteemed colleague,
I write from the Snowclad Ruins with three working fingers. The wall here bears a Word in the dragon tongue, which I have copied, and which I believe concerns ice, or the becoming of ice. I have not been able to speak it aloud. I suspect I am meant to be unable.

One further observation, which I set down at the risk of your ridicule: the snow here does not drift against the wall. It drifts around it, in a perfect ring, as if the wall were warm. It is not warm. I touched it. I am still waking at night with the shape of the letters in my palm. Yours, in some distress, Aurelian.

notes.title: Bone Wind-Chime Note
pages: Tied to a chime of horker bones on the ruin's arch: Skaal walk around this place, not through it. The wall speaks to dragons, and dragons answer. If the chimes are ringing and there is no wind, walk faster.

On the other side of the bark, a fainter line: The scholar from the mainland did not walk faster. He sat down by the wall and stayed there all night with his eyes open, saying a word over and over. We carried him to Raven Rock. He still says it in his sleep, and the candle flames bend when he does.

moesring_pass.hook: The high road over the Moesring mountains, the only way between the island's ash-grey south and its frozen north for anyone without wings. It is narrow, windy, and watched.
moesring_pass.rumour: Take Moesring Pass in the morning, never at dusk. The wind up there pushes. A Company porter went over the edge last Last Seed, pack and all. They found the pack.

notes.title: Waymarker on the Pass
pages: Painted on a slab at the narrowest point, in Cyrodilic and in Skaal runes both: North lies the snow, south lies the ash. The wind changes at noon. Walk with your shoulder to the mountain. Do not stop here to look at the view of Mount Moesring; the view does not care for you. Three porters, one Telvanni apprentice, and a goat have taught us this. The goat survived.

Beneath it someone has added, with a knife: Also do not stop to look at the bones in the ravine. They are mostly goat. Mostly. If you hear rocks falling above you, that is not the wind either. That is rieklings, and they think it is very funny.

fahlbtharz.hook: A Dwemer ruin west of Mount Moesring whose steam pipes have hissed without pause for four thousand years. A Company prospector went in for the boilers' brass and came out with burns and a theory.
fahlbtharz.rumour: Fahlbtharz breathes. You can see the steam from the pass on a cold morning. A Company man went in, came out scalded, went back in. Must be some theory.

notes.title: Prospector's Journal, Water-Stained
notes.author: Decimus Vello, East Empire Company prospector
pages:
#2nd of Frostfall
The pipes run hot through the whole upper hall. Every valve I have found is set to the same mark. The Dwemer did not leave this place running by accident; they left it running on purpose. Whatever needs this much steam is still waiting for it.

#4th of Frostfall
Found the regulator: a brass heart the size of a ram's skull, fitted into the central pipe. It hums. When I touched it the whole ruin shuddered and something big stood up in the lower hall. Steam came out of its joints. It looked at me. I left.

#5th of Frostfall
The regulator would buy me out of my Company contract twice over. It is guarded by a centurion that the steam keeps warm and awake. Need a fighter. Will try Raven Rock. Will try anyone.

notes.title: Translated Dwemer Plate
notes.author: Ulvo Nerano (translation)
pages:
A thin brass plate, with a scholar's translation pinned to it: Pressure is maintained so that the guardian is maintained. The guardian is maintained so that pressure is maintained. Do not disturb the regulator without the consent of the Tonal Assembly.
The scholar's marginal note: The Tonal Assembly has not met in four thousand years. I believe we may consider its consent lapsed.

A further scribble in another hand, likely the prospector Decimus Vello: Nerano, if your translation is correct, removing the regulator stops the guardian. If it is wrong, removing the regulator angers the guardian. Kindly be correct.

mount_moesring.hook: The great grey mountain at the island's heart, split by the Moesring Pass. Ash drifts on its southern slopes and snow on its northern, and on the summit they meet.
mount_moesring.rumour: From the top of Mount Moesring you can see Red Mountain smoking across the sea. My mother says the mountain is looking back at us, the way it did in the Red Year.

notes.title: Summit Diary of a Redoran Guard
notes.author: Varona Sethri
pages:
#8th of Last Seed
Climbed on my day of leave. South, the island is black and grey to the shore, and beyond the water Red Mountain is still smoking, as if it had only just done the thing it did. North, everything is white. Up here the ash falls into the snow and makes it look like a ledger with too many entries.

I thought about my grandfather, who left Vvardenfell the year the sky fell, and about how far a person can run and still see the thing behind them. I left a stone for him at the top. Then I walked down to Raven Rock and took the night watch, because that is what we do.

altar_of_thrond.hook: A weathered stone altar between Mount Moesring and the Temple of Miraak, older than the Skaal. Offerings left here vanish overnight, and no one admits to taking them.
altar_of_thrond.rumour: Leave something at the Altar of Thrond and it's gone by morning. Skaal say Thrond takes it. Raven Rock folk say rieklings. My coin's on rieklings.

notes.title: Worn Carving on the Altar
pages:
Old Nordic letters, half eaten by ash and frost, with a translation scratched beneath by some visitor: To Thrond, who stood between the island and the dragon-masked ones and would not kneel. Bring him salt, bread, and a true word. He was the last who said no.
Below, in a different hand, fresh: The masked ones have been here. They left nothing. They broke the bread. The altar is not happy.
And lower, carved deliberately by a Skaal hand: We brought new bread. Thrond, forgive the breakers. They follow one who knelt to everyone and everything, and he will kneel to them in the end.

temple_of_miraak.hook: A great ruined temple rising from the stone west of Thirsk, built in the Dragon Priests' age. Sleepwalkers have come here from Raven Rock, and not every family has found its missing.
temple_of_miraak.rumour: Folk from Raven Rock walk out to the Temple of Miraak in their sleep. Most come home. Durel Rendas's wife Mirisa walked there last month and they haven't found her yet. The Guard says she's not inside. They didn't look very hard.

notes.title: Note Tucked into a Crack in the Wall
notes.author: Durel Rendas of Raven Rock
pages:
Mirisa,
If you are inside and you wake up, if you find this: I came. I came every night for a week. The masked ones would not let me down the stairs. I left bread and your shawl by the door. The shawl is gone. I choose to believe you took it.
The Guard says to wait. Sergeant Indaram says the sleepers come home on their own. Some of them do. Come home, Mirisa. The kettle is on. The kettle is always on now. Durel.

notes.title: Labour Roster of the Faithful
pages:
Sleepers assigned to the outer stair: eleven. Stone-carriers: six. Two collapsed on the third night; return them to the Earth Stone road where the Guard will find them. The Master has no use for broken tools.
The Faithful are reminded that the masks are not to be removed in the presence of sleepers. They remember faces in their dreams, though not on waking. Brother Ulfgar is at Hrothmund's Barrow seeking the key and is not to be disturbed.
In the margin, a smaller hand: Durel Rendas comes every night to the outer door. He has seen his wife on the stair twice. Kill him, or let him join the sleepers. The Master does not care which.

bujolds_retreat.hook: A Nord homestead on the eastern coast, abandoned by the family who built it and taken over by reavers. They raid the Skaal sledges and sell what they steal on the docks at Raven Rock.
bujolds_retreat.rumour: Reavers at Bujold's Retreat stole a Skaal hunting mask older than my village. The Skaal won't fight for it. Not their way, they say. I'd fight for my grandfather's face.

notes.title: Orders from the Gut-Hook
notes.author: Halvar Gut-Hook
pages:
Listen, you sea-lice. The Skaal don't fight. That's the beauty of it. They pray at you and walk off. So we take what we like off their sledges, and nobody in Raven Rock asks where the furs came from.
The mask stays here. Some Telvanni at Tel Mithryn will pay forty drakes for anything the Skaal think is holy. I'll sell it myself. Anyone who tries to sell it first gets to swim to Windhelm.

Watch the north path toward Gyldenhul Barrow. If a Skaal comes with a spear, run. If anyone else comes with a spear, kill them. If anyone comes with an axe and a hammer and a look in their eye, wake me up first.

notes.title: Old Letter Under the Floorboards
notes.author: Bujold
pages: To whoever lives here after me: I built this house to be away from Thirsk and its quarrels. It is a good house. The roof does not leak and the hearth draws well. Treat it kindly. If you are a quarreller yourself, go back to Thirsk. If you are worse than a quarreller, the house will know, and so will the Skaal, and so will I, wherever I have gone.

The ink is old, and beneath it a reaver has drawn a rude picture of a woman with a bucket on her head. Underneath that, in yet another hand, very small: The hearth does draw well. The roof does not leak. I am sorry, Bujold. I would leave if I could.

frostmoon_crag.hook: A crag in the highlands west of the Altar of Thrond where wolves that are not wolves gather under the full moon. The hunting lodge downhill has been empty since the night they gathered for its keeper.
frostmoon_crag.rumour: Don't camp near Frostmoon Crag. The Skaal say Hircine's children run there under the full moon. The fellow who kept the Abandoned Lodge used to laugh at that story.

notes.title: Claw-Marks Around a Bone Totem
pages: Scratched into a pine by something with claws, and then, more carefully, by something with a knife: The Hunt does not end. The moon calls and we answer. The man from the lodge answered. He did not want to, at first. Now he runs at the head of the pack and does not remember his own name. We call him Grey Brother. He keeps a ring on a thong around his throat and growls at anyone who looks at it.

notes.title: Skaal Hunter's Mark
pages: Painted on a flat stone below the crag in red earth, a Skaal warning of the kind they leave for each other: Moon-beasts here. Do not hunt alone. Do not hunt at night. If one of them speaks to you, do not answer. If one of them speaks to you in the voice of someone you knew, run, and do not look back to see whose face it is wearing.

Beneath the red marks, someone has scratched a name: Sigvar. Then a line through it, not quite finished, as though whoever began it could not decide whether a man who runs with the pack is dead or only gone.

damphall_mine.hook: A Raven Rock mine in the western hills, abandoned after a seam of hot water broke through the lower galleries. The steam brought up more than water: the ash itself has started walking there.
damphall_mine.rumour: Damphall Mine was a good dig until the water came up boiling. Now the miners say there's ash spawn in the lower galleries, climbing out of the steam like it's birthing them.

notes.title: Last Shift Report, Damphall Mine
notes.author: Overseer Rels Llarys
pages:
#Turdas, 9th of Sun's Dusk
Water broke through at the third gallery at mid-shift. Scalding. Two men burned, no deaths. Pumps cannot keep up. Withdrew to the second gallery.
#Fredas, 10th
Something moved in the steam. Not a man. Grey, crusted, burning at the joints. It walked straight out of the water as if the water had made it. Then another.

#Loredas, 11th
Mine closed by my order. The payroll chest is still in the overseer's alcove in the lower gallery: one hundred and twelve drakes owed to eleven miners who have families on the Raven Rock docks. I am not going back for it. I am ashamed to write that. If anyone else goes, take the payroll to Sergeant Indaram, who will see it fairly paid.

notes.title: Scratched on a Support Beam
pages: Scratched with the point of a pick, in Dunmeri: Ash is the bones of our grandmothers, my mother said. Then why are our grandmothers trying to kill us? Under it, another hand: Because we dug them up without asking. Under that, a third: Because we didn't pay them. Ha. Under that, nothing more, and a long scorch-mark across the wood.

At the very bottom, almost hidden by soot, in a careful hand: Rels Llarys owes me two weeks. Rels Llarys owes all of us. If anyone ever brings the payroll out, tell my wife on the docks that I did not run first.

hvitkald_peak.hook: A white peak north of Raven Rock, standing over the Abandoned Lodge. Ash and snow streak its flanks in grey bands, and from its top the whole southern coast lies open.
hvitkald_peak.rumour: Hvitkald Peak. The Nords named it white-cold. Since the Red Year it's been more grey-cold. The view's still good, if you like looking at ash.

notes.title: Lookout Post Report
notes.author: Guardsman Tolvyn Arethi
pages: To Sergeant Indaram. Lookout on Hvitkald, third day. Smoke from the Abandoned Lodge chimney last night, though the lodge has stood empty since Frostfall. No smoke this morning. Wolf howls from the direction of Frostmoon Crag, many, at moonrise. Torchlight moving on the barrow road toward Bloodskal Barrow, four or five lights. Grave robbers, I think, not draugr; draugr do not need torches. Requesting relief. Requesting a warmer cloak. Requesting that the relief bring the cloak.
Postscript: The sergeant should know that Helga from the docks walked past my post again this Loredas, carrying boots up to the lodge. I told her it was empty. She said she knew. She went anyway.

abandoned_lodge.hook: A hunting lodge below Hvitkald Peak, its door hanging open and its larder untouched. The hunter who lived here walked out one full moon and did not come back as himself.
abandoned_lodge.rumour: The Abandoned Lodge belonged to a hunter called Sigvar. Good shot, bad temper. Went out under the full moon chasing a white wolf toward Frostmoon Crag and never came home. His wife's still waiting in Raven Rock.

notes.title: Sigvar's Hunting Journal
notes.author: Sigvar the Lodge-Keeper
pages:
#12th of Frostfall
A white wolf took the doe off my line again, right under my nose, and looked back at me as it went. Not like a wolf looks. Like a man looks when he's won at dice.

#14th of Frostfall
Followed its tracks to Frostmoon Crag. More tracks there than I could count. Some wolf, some man, some that start as one and end as the other. Went home and drank. Have not told Helga.

#15th of Frostfall
Full moon tonight. I am going back. My ring from Helga is on the thong around my neck, where it always is. If I do not come home, she should have it back. I keep thinking about the white wolf's eyes. They looked like they knew me.

notes.title: Letter Left on the Table
notes.author: Helga
pages:
Sigvar,
I came up from Raven Rock with your winter boots and found the door open and the fire cold. I am leaving the boots by the hearth. I am leaving this letter on the table, where you will see it when you come home. I will come back every Loredas until you do. Do not make me come every Loredas forever. Your Helga.

A second sheet beneath the first, the ink fresher: Fourth Loredas. The boots are gone from the hearth. The door was shut from outside. There were wolf tracks all round the lodge, and one set of a man's bare feet, going toward Frostmoon Crag. Sigvar, if that was you, why did you not knock?

vahloks_tomb.hook: The sealed tomb of Vahlok the Jailor, a dragon priest who stood guard against his own kind in the old days. Scholars want rubbings from its walls; its guardians want them to leave.
vahloks_tomb.rumour: Vahlok's Tomb belongs to a dragon priest who turned warden. A scholar from Tel Mithryn sent his assistant to take rubbings of the walls. The assistant came back without the rubbings and without his eyebrows.

notes.title: Assistant's Report to Ulvo Nerano
notes.author: Fendryn Llaro, assistant
pages:
Master Nerano,
As instructed I entered the Jailor's tomb with charcoal, paper, and a very good lantern. I took eleven rubbings of the inscriptions in the long hall. They describe an oath sworn by Vahlok to keep a certain prisoner from ever returning to the world. The prisoner is not named. Everyone in the inscriptions is extremely careful not to name him.

At the twelfth rubbing the dead woke up. I ran, and dropped the satchel with all eleven rubbings in the long hall, beside the brazier with the dragon carved on it. I will not be going back. I would like to discuss my wages. Fendryn.

notes.title: Fragment of the Jailor's Oath
pages:
Cut into the stone above the sarcophagus, in old Nordic, with a translation pencilled beneath by a living hand: I who served the dragons will watch the one who betrayed them. I will not sleep while he sleeps. I will not wake until he wakes. Let the island be my cell and his, and let my bones be the bars.
In the margin: He has started waking, then. I don't like that at all.

Under the pencil, scrawled in charcoal by a different scholar: Ulvo, do not send another assistant here. The Jailor is awake, and he is not angry with us. He is afraid. A dragon priest afraid. Think about that before you publish anything.

kagrumez.hook: A Dwemer ruin whose resonance chambers still sing, west of the dragon burial mound. The Dwemer built it to test something with sound; the gems still answer anyone who strikes them.
kagrumez.rumour: Kagrumez sings. I mean it. You stand at the door and you can hear the stones humming. Some Telvanni scholar is desperate to know what tune.

notes.title: Notes on the Resonance Chambers
notes.author: Ulvo Nerano
pages: Each chamber holds plinths. Each plinth holds a gem, or held one; most are scattered. Placed correctly, the gems sound together and a door opens. Placed incorrectly, the guardians wake. I placed them incorrectly. Twice.

The theory: the Dwemer made the chambers to train the ear, or perhaps to train the soul, in the tones that hold the world together. The practice: there is a tuning key, a brass fork as long as my forearm, in the deepest chamber. With it one can read the correct tones without guessing. My wager is that the key still lies on the master plinth. My other wager is that I will not survive to collect on the first.

notes.title: Scrap Hunter's Scrawl
pages: Chalked on a pipe, in a sloppy hand: Wrong gem, the spiders come. Wrong gem twice, the big ball comes. Wrong gem three times and you are me, sitting behind a pipe writing this with chalk while something rolls up and down the hall looking for you. Do not take the shiny ones in the first room. They are the wrong ones. They are always the wrong ones.

Under it, in different chalk: Burzol at the Ramshackle Trading Post buys the gears for twenty drakes. Tel Mithryn buys them from Burzol for eighty. Cut out the Orc. Also, do not cut out the Orc where he can hear you.

bloodskal_barrow.hook: A Nordic barrow north of Raven Rock, cut with red-stained stone. Grave robbers have been digging there by torchlight, and Raven Rock's own ancestral urns have started turning up in their sacks.
bloodskal_barrow.rumour: Grave robbers at Bloodskal Barrow. The Guard says they've been stealing urns out of our own tomb in town and stashing them in the barrow before shipping out. Stealing a Dunmer's ancestors. There's no lower thing.

notes.title: Grave Robbers' Inventory
notes.author: Fevyn the Scrapper
pages:
From the town tomb: four urns, decent glaze, one cracked. Sell to the Khajiit at the docks, who will sell to some fool in Cyrodiil who thinks Dunmer ashes are a cure for gout.
One urn of the Morvayn line, silver-banded. Keep that one apart. The Councilor's family will pay to get it back quietly, and pay more to keep it quiet.

From the barrow itself: copper, bronze, rotten furs, two Nord swords, one of them good. The rest of the deep rooms are sealed with a red stone door that won't open for any lever we've found. Henrik says it hums. Henrik is drunk. Leave the deep rooms alone.

notes.title: Guard Report on the Tomb Thefts
notes.author: Mileth Indaram
pages: To the Councilor. Five urns are missing from the ancestral tomb, one of them from your own family's niche. The thieves came through the drainage cut on the west wall. Tracks lead north toward Bloodskal Barrow. I recommend that we send a party of four. I recognise that we do not have four to spare, and that the Bulwark comes first. I will therefore ask outsiders, and I will keep the matter quiet, as you will wish. Indaram.

Appended in the Councilor's own hand: Do what you think best, Sergeant. Bring my grandmother home. I will not ask how. I will not ask who. I will ask only that she be home before the Feast of the Dead.

brodir_grove.hook: A grove of ancient trees in the ash wastes north of Raven Rock, one of the few green places left in the south. The spriggans here have grown restless since Telvanni gatherers came with sickles.
brodir_grove.rumour: Brodir Grove used to be a nice place for a picnic. Then some Telvanni apprentices came cutting bark for their master's potions, and now the trees walk.

notes.title: Gathering List from Tel Mithryn
notes.author: Talvas Fathryon
pages:
For the master's preparation, gather at Brodir Grove:
Bark from the eldest tree, three palms' width. Sap, one phial. Moss from the north face, as much as will fill a pouch.
The master says the spriggans will not mind. The master has not been to Brodir Grove in thirty years. Bring a fire spell. Bring two. If the trees start singing, do not stop to listen, it is not a compliment.
At the bottom, in a hurried hand: Gathered the bark. The eldest tree screamed. Ran. Left the sickle. Left one boot. If the master wants the moss, the master can come and get it himself.

notes.title: Offering Bundle in the Roots
pages: A twist of birch bark tucked into the roots of the eldest tree, with a few dried berries and a lock of hair. The words cut in the bark: Grandmother Tree, forgive the sickle-men. They do not know the All-Maker made you before he made them. We have brought you water from the Headwaters of Harstrad and a song. Be patient with them. Be patient with us. We will be gone before you are.

Tied with the bark, a twist of red wool and a second strip, more recent: The Telvanni sickle-man came back. He left his own offering this time: a phial of good wine and a note in his tongue. We cannot read it, but the tree let him go, so it must have been an apology.

ramshackle_trading_post.hook: A wind-battered trading post on the road between Kagrumez and the coast, run by an Orc who buys anything and asks nothing. Half the stolen goods on the island pass across his counter.
ramshackle_trading_post.rumour: The Ramshackle Trading Post buys anything. Dwemer scrap, Skaal furs, a riekling's spear, your mother's teeth. The Orc who runs it doesn't ask where any of it came from, and you shouldn't ask where it goes.

notes.title: Trading Post Ledger
notes.author: Mogrul's cousin Burzol
pages:
Bought: Dwemer gears, four, from a Dunmer with singed eyebrows who came from Kagrumez. 20 drakes. Sold same to Tel Mithryn for 80.
Bought: furs, Skaal-made, eleven, from a reaver who said they were his. They were not his. 30 drakes. Sold to the Company for 90.
Bought: one silver-banded ash urn, Dunmer, from a fellow called Fevyn. Refused. Some things have a curse on them even when they haven't.

Note to self: the reavers at Bujold's Retreat owe me for two casks of mead and a new boat. Do not sell them anything else until they pay. Do not tell them where I keep the strongbox. Do not let Gnaw-Tooth's rieklings near the mead, whatever they offer to trade. Last time they offered me a horker. A live horker.

ashfallow_citadel.hook: A walled Telvanni citadel in the ash wastes east of Kagrumez, held by a renegade wizard who quarrelled with Neloth. She has found a way to make the ash itself stand up and serve.
ashfallow_citadel.rumour: Ashfallow Citadel's got a new mistress. Telvanni, cast out of Tel Mithryn. They say she can raise ash spawn the way a farmer raises guar. And she's not raising them to plough.

notes.title: Research Notes of Seryne Dralas
notes.author: Seryne Dralas
pages: Neloth said the ash spawn are a nuisance to be swept from doorsteps. Neloth is old and lazy and has never asked what the ash remembers. I have. It remembers being people. It remembers the Red Year. It remembers a great deal of anger, and anger can be shaped.

Progress: seven risen, all obedient. A heart-stone of compressed ash at the core of each gives them purpose. I need more ash. Raven Rock has a great deal of it, swept into piles every morning by the Redoran fools. When I have thirty, I will go and collect it. When I have a hundred, I will go and collect Tel Mithryn.
Personal: Neloth's spies watch from the Sun Stone. Let them watch. Let them tell him. I want him to know it was me.

notes.title: Unsent Letter of a Hired Guard
notes.author: Jorund
pages:
Ma,
The wizard pays well. Better than the mine at Raven Rock, better than fishing. The work is standing on a wall and watching for Telvanni.
The things she makes walk the yard at night. They do not sleep. They do not eat. They stand by the gate and look south toward Raven Rock, all of them, the same way, like dogs that smell supper.
I am going to leave before she makes enough of them to need us gone. If I do not come, burn this, and do not tell Pa what I was doing here. Tell him I was fishing. Jorund.

notes.title: Citadel Supply List
pages: Needed from the Ramshackle Trading Post: salt fish, 30. Sujamma, 4 bottles, the good kind, not the kind Burzol waters. Soul gems, any size, as many as he has. Lamp oil. New lock for the south gate. Tell Burzol the Mistress will pay at the end of the month. Tell Burzol not to ask about the end of the month.

Underneath, scrawled by a guard: Burzol says no more credit until the Mistress pays for the last lot. The Mistress says Burzol will be paid in ash. I do not think she was joking, and I do not think he knows what that means.

nchardak.hook: A great Dwemer ruin on the eastern coast, half drowned and still humming with steam. Treasure hunters, Telvanni scholars, and worse all have business in its flooded halls.
nchardak.rumour: Nchardak's full of water and machines and books nobody should read. Master Neloth goes there sometimes. Comes back muttering. Everyone else who goes comes back wet, if they come back.

notes.title: Waterlogged Journal
notes.author: Erith Varanu
pages:
#20th of Hearthfire
The water rises and falls in the great hall when you turn the cubes in the pedestals. Nobody told me that. Nobody told me the water has slaughterfish in it, either, four thousand years old and still hungry.

#22nd of Hearthfire
Found a sealed room at the heart of the ruin with a book on a lectern, and a Telvanni seal on the door that is much newer than the Dwemer stone around it. I did not open the book. I did not open the door. I have heard what happens to people who read the wrong books on this island. They go to sleep and walk somewhere, and they don't come back.

notes.title: Telvanni Seal Notice
pages: Burned into a brass plate fixed to the inner door, in elegant Telvanni script: This ruin is under the study of Master Neloth of Tel Mithryn. Removal of anything without the master's consent will be noticed. Being noticed by the master is not recommended. Being noticed twice is not survivable. This notice is the only one you will receive.
Scratched beneath the plate with a knife point, in Cyrodilic: Noted. Twice. Signed, a visitor who now has one ear fewer. And beneath that, burned neatly into the brass: Three times.

highpoint_tower.hook: A slender Telvanni tower on a crag north of Fort Frostmoth, grown and then abandoned by a wizard who wanted to watch Red Mountain. Something he summoned to guard it is still on watch.
highpoint_tower.rumour: Highpoint Tower was some Telvanni's observatory. He left, and his guardian didn't. The Redoran Guard won't go up there. They say the stairs move.

notes.title: Observation Log of Arvyn Hlervu
notes.author: Arvyn Hlervu, Telvanni wizard
pages:
#Night of the 3rd, Rain's Hand
Red Mountain glows tonight, faintly. My instruments say the fire under it is not dead, only sleeping, the way a wounded man sleeps. I have recorded the glow on fourteen nights this season. Neloth says I am wasting my talents. Neloth says that about every talent he does not have.

#Night of the 9th
Bound a guardian of fire and ash to the tower. It will keep my instruments and my grimoire safe while I sail to Sadrith Mora to present my findings. It understands only one instruction: let no one up the stair who is not me.
Final entry, scrawled in haste: Recalled to Vvardenfell by my house. I will return in a month. The grimoire stays in the top chamber. The guardian stays with it.

notes.title: Guardsman's Note on Highpoint
notes.author: Tolvyn Arethi
pages: Sergeant, as asked, I looked at Highpoint Tower. The door is open. The stairs go up. Something burning walks round and round the top chamber and does not stop. The Telvanni who built it left eleven years ago, according to the Company records, and did not come back. The thing upstairs is still waiting for him. I did not go up. I would like that noted as wisdom, not cowardice.
Postscript: There is a lamp lit in the top window every night at the hour the wizard used to look at the mountain. Nobody climbs up to light it. I would also like that noted.

kolbjorn_barrow.hook: An old Nordic barrow half buried by ash a short walk from Raven Rock. Diggers paid by the hopeful excavator Ralis Sedarys are clearing it a bucket at a time, and not all of them come up again at dusk.
kolbjorn_barrow.rumour: Kolbjorn Barrow's being dug out by that Dunmer, Ralis Sedarys. Paying good coin, when he pays. Tilvur Sadas's boy Neral went down a week ago and hasn't come up. Ralis says he's fine. Ralis says everything's fine.

notes.title: Neral's Digging Diary
notes.author: Neral Sadas
pages:
#Middas
Cleared six buckets of ash from the second gallery. Found a Nord bracelet, bronze, gave it to the foreman like an honest fool. Father would be proud. Father would also want the wages.

#Fredas
Broke through to a side chamber behind the second gallery. Old bones in the niches. Some of them turned their heads when my lantern passed. I am not mad. Varis saw it too.

#Sundas
The gallery fell in behind us. Varis got out. I am in the side chamber with a lantern, half a loaf, and my pass from Sergeant Indaram. The bones are standing up. If someone finds this before they find me, I am behind the third pillar, and I would very much like to go home.

notes.title: Diggers Wanted
notes.author: Ralis Sedarys
pages:
^Diggers Wanted at Kolbjorn Barrow
Strong backs and short memories required. Wages paid on reaching the inner door, with a bonus for each artefact handed over intact. The Redoran Guard has been informed and has expressed no objection, or at least no objection I could hear over the wind. Apply at the dig. Bring your own shovel. Bring your own lantern. Bring, if you have one, your own courage; the barrow supplies none.

Scrawled across the bottom by some disgruntled digger: Wages paid on reaching the inner door. We have not reached the inner door. We will never reach the inner door. The inner door, Ralis, is a lie you tell yourself.

fort_frostmoth.hook: The broken shell of an Imperial Legion fort on the southern coast, shattered when Red Mountain burst. Its legionaries never left their posts, and on ash-heavy nights they still stand to.
fort_frostmoth.rumour: Fort Frostmoth died the day the mountain blew. The legionaries were at their posts and stayed there. Old Aulus Vettrius at Raven Rock says his brother went in to fetch the cohort's standard home and hasn't been seen since.

notes.title: Last Muster of Fort Frostmoth
notes.author: Optio Quintus Salvius
pages:
#Morning report, 4E 5
Present and fit: thirty-one. Sick: four. The sky over Vvardenfell has turned the colour of an old bruise. The fishermen say the sea is warm. The Captain has ordered that the standard be kept in the inner hall and the men stand to at the walls.

#Evening report
Ash falling like snow, hot. The shore is burning. The ships cannot put out. The Captain says the Legion does not leave its posts without orders, and we have no orders, because no ship can reach us to bring them. Present and fit: thirty-one. We will stand to. The standard will not fall while one of us is standing.

notes.title: Letter from Gaius Vettrius
notes.author: Gaius Vettrius
pages:
Aulus,
I am in the old fort. Our great-grandfather's name is cut into the wall of the inner hall with the others. I read it aloud, and something in the dark answered with the muster call.

They are still here, brother. Bones in rusted plate, standing to. The standard is in the inner hall, where the reports say it was. I tried to take it, and the officer's shade stood up from his chair and put himself between me and it. I am hurt. I will try again at dawn. If I do not come back, the standard should go home, and so should they. Gaius.

notes.title: Redoran Survey of the Ruin
notes.author: Raven Rock Guard
pages: The fort's walls are sound on the seaward side only. Ash spawn are often seen in the courtyard, drawn, the old Guard say, to the Imperial dead the way the ash is drawn to anything that burned. The Councilor has decided that the fort is not Redoran business. Imperials who wish to visit their dead may do so at their own risk. We have warned them. We have warned them several times.

Added later: An Imperial named Gaius Vettrius passed the Bulwark in Frostfall, bound for the fort. He was warned. He showed us his family's Legion ring and said his great-grandfather was still on duty. The watch laughed. Nobody is laughing now.

hrodulfs_house.hook: A Nord's lonely cottage on the southern coast, between Fort Frostmoth and the sea. Its owner left in the middle of the night, barefoot, and walked north toward the stones.
hrodulfs_house.rumour: Hrodulf's House has stood empty since Hrodulf walked off in his sleep. The door was found wide open, the fire still lit, and his boots by the bed. Nobody's touched it since.

notes.title: Hrodulf's Night Journal
notes.author: Hrodulf
pages:
#First night
Woke at the door with my hand on the latch. Cold floor, no memory. Wrote it down so I would not think I dreamed it.
#Fourth night
Woke on the path toward Raven Rock with mud to the knee. There was a voice in my sleep, patient and kind. It said I was building something important.

#Ninth night
I tied my ankle to the bedpost with a rope. Woke with the rope cut cleanly and a sharp stone in my hand. I do not own a knife that sharp.
#Last entry
The voice says I am nearly finished. It says the work is beautiful. I believe it. I do not want to believe it. Whoever reads this: do not sleep in this house.

wreck_of_the_strident_squall.hook: The broken hull of the Strident Squall on the island's southern shore, picked over by wreckers and mudcrabs. The Company wanted its strongbox; the cook only ever wanted his savings.
wreck_of_the_strident_squall.rumour: The Strident Squall? The Company sent folk for the pay chest. Nobody went looking for Old Fennick's savings, though. He was the ship's cook, and he never trusted a strongbox in his life.

notes.title: Cook's Letter in a Bottle
notes.author: Fennick the cook
pages:
To my sister Ottilie in Anvil, if this bottle ever floats that far:
We hit the rocks in the dark. The captain is shouting about the Company's box. I have no box. I have a little sea-chest of my own, thirty years of wages in it, and I have dragged it up the beach and buried it in the shingle below the big black rock, about thirty paces inland from the bow, where the tide never reaches.

The wreckers are coming down the cliff with lanterns. I am going to swim for it. If I make Raven Rock, I will go back for the chest myself. If I do not, Ottilie, it is yours. Buy that little house by the lighthouse. Fennick.

notes.title: Wreckers' Share Agreement
pages: Everything off the Squall split even, after the lantern-man takes his tenth. Company goods go to the Orc at the Ramshackle Trading Post, who doesn't ask. Personal goods we keep. The Company will send someone for their box, so we leave the box, and we leave quickly when the sails come. Nobody digs on the beach. Somebody saw the cook digging. Somebody should have dug faster.

Addendum, in a different hand: The cook did not come back. Neither did the lantern-man, who went looking for the cook's hole on his own. The tide brought his lantern back. If anyone finds the big black rock, share, or swim.

allmaker_water_stone.hook: One of the six stones of the All-Maker, raised by the Skaal in the island's west. The Skaal come to it for the blessing of the sea and the rivers. Lately they come to it frightened.
allmaker_water_stone.rumour: The Water Stone's sick, the Skaal say. Some kind of wall's grown up around it overnight. My cousin heard chanting from there, and he says nobody was chanting.

notes.title: Prayer at the Water Stone
pages:
~All-Maker, who gave the fish its river and the river its sea,
~Who froze the sea to give the Skaal a road,
~Keep the water moving, that it may not grow bitter;
~Keep us moving, that we may not grow bitter.
~The stone is cold tonight, and something sits beside it
~Who is not you. Do not let it drink.

Beneath the verse a Skaal fisher has cut: Three nights ago, the stream that runs by the stone flowed backward for an hour. I put my hand in it and it was warm. Storn says the stone is sick. I say it is frightened.

allmaker_earth_stone.hook: The All-Maker's Earth Stone, west of Raven Rock, where sleepwalkers from the town have built a strange shrine around the ancient pillar without knowing they did it.
allmaker_earth_stone.rumour: The sleepwalkers go to the Earth Stone, carry rocks, build walls, and come home with no memory of it. Every morning the shrine is a little taller.

notes.title: Night Watch at the Earth Stone
notes.author: Varona Sethri, Redoran Guard
pages: Sergeant, as ordered, I watched the Earth Stone from the ridge from dusk until dawn. Fourteen townsfolk arrived after midnight, some barefoot, all silent. I recognised Ilvi Sadrano, the smith's apprentice, and two of the Company miners. They worked without speaking, setting stone on stone, as neatly as masons.

When I went down to turn Ilvi home, she looked at me and smiled and said: we are nearly done. Then she went back to work. At first light they all simply stopped and walked back to town, and when I asked them at the gate what they had been doing, every one of them said they had been asleep. I believe them. I do not know what to report.

allmaker_tree_stone.hook: The All-Maker's Tree Stone, standing just north of the Temple of Miraak. The Skaal bring it the first green of spring; something else has been bringing it a shadow.
allmaker_tree_stone.rumour: The Tree Stone is right next to the Temple of Miraak. Skaal say that was never a coincidence, and that the stone's been fighting the temple for a thousand years. And losing, lately.

notes.title: Skaal Offering Tag
pages: A strip of bark tied to the base of the stone, with Skaal runes burned into it: For the Tree Stone, from the children of Brandvar's hearth. A sprig of pine, the first of the season, though the season is late. The roots of the trees near the temple have turned black this year. We do not know why. We have brought our sprig anyway. Even a sick stone needs its offering.

On the reverse: The pine we left last spring has turned grey, though no frost could touch it here. The temple stones grow a little higher every night. The Tree Stone is the oldest thing on this hill, older than the temple, and it is tired.

allmaker_beast_stone.hook: The All-Maker's Beast Stone, a short walk west of Thirsk Mead Hall. Skaal hunters touch it before a hunt. Lately, the beasts themselves have been coming to it and standing very still.
allmaker_beast_stone.rumour: A Thirsk hunter told me he saw a bear, a wolf and a horker standing at the Beast Stone side by side, just staring at it. Not fighting. Staring. Then they all walked away north together.

notes.title: Thirsk Hunter's Observations
notes.author: Gunnar of Thirsk
pages: Three mornings running I have found tracks of many beasts circling the Beast Stone and not one of them hunting another. Rabbit beside wolf, wolf beside bear. On the third morning I waited. They came at dusk, stood around the stone like folk at a funeral, and left in the same direction: toward the Temple of Miraak. I did not follow. Brenna says I should tell the Skaal. The Skaal already know. They just look at me and say the stone is sick.

allmaker_wind_stone.hook: The All-Maker's Wind Stone, on the high ground west of the Skaal village. The Skaal say the wind carries their prayers from here. Lately it carries a voice they do not know.
allmaker_wind_stone.rumour: The Skaal won't go near the Wind Stone any more. They say the wind speaks there, and it's not the All-Maker speaking.

notes.title: Chant of the Wind Stone
pages:
~Wind of the north, carry our words,
~Over the ice to the All-Maker's ear.
~Wind of the north, carry our dead,
~Over the sea where the stars are near.

Scratched underneath by a younger hand: The wind is wrong this winter. It blows from the stone and not toward it. When I put my hand on the stone I heard someone say my name, and then say that I would be useful. I did not tell Storn. I am telling the stone instead. Stone, tell the All-Maker.

allmaker_sun_stone.hook: The All-Maker's Sun Stone, on the ash plain north of Tel Mithryn. The Skaal greet the dawn here. Telvanni spies watch the road to Ashfallow Citadel from its shadow.
allmaker_sun_stone.rumour: There's a Telvanni apprentice who spends all day sitting in the shade of the Sun Stone with a spyglass, looking at Ashfallow Citadel. Says it's research. Looks like spying to me.

notes.title: Observer's Report to Tel Mithryn
notes.author: Aldryn Varo, apprentice
pages: To the master's steward. From the Sun Stone, fourth day. The renegade Seryne Dralas walks the walls of Ashfallow Citadel at dawn and dusk. I have counted seven ash creatures in her yard; today there were nine. They face south toward Raven Rock and do not move. Her hired guards appear nervous, which I consider sensible of them.

Additional: the Sun Stone itself is unwell. The Skaal who come to greet the sunrise here touch it and pull their hands away as if it burned. At night I hear stone grinding against stone, but there is nobody here except me. I would like to be relieved. I would like to be relieved quite soon.

dragon_mound_glacial_cave.hook: An ancient dragon burial mound on the frozen northern coast, beyond the Glacial Cave. The Skaal shunned it for centuries; this winter the earth over it has split open.
dragon_mound_glacial_cave.rumour: The dragon mound past the Glacial Cave is open. Empty. A Skaal hunter saw the wings go up out of it at night, black against the aurora.

notes.title: Skaal Hunter's Account
notes.author: Finna Seal-Daughter
pages: I was hunting seal on the ice when the ground shook. I saw a man in a mask standing on the mound, though there are no men out here, and he spoke, and the mound answered. Bones came up out of the earth and put on flesh as I watched. Then it flew north, and the man in the mask was gone, and I ran all the way to the village. Storn listened and said nothing for a long time, and then he went to the stones.

dragon_mound_kagrumez.hook: A dragon burial mound in the ash hills east of Kagrumez. The Telvanni once studied it and the Skaal once avoided it. Now there is nothing in it at all.
dragon_mound_kagrumez.rumour: The dragon mound near Kagrumez is a hole in the ground now. Some say a Telvanni dug it up for research. Others say something climbed out by itself.

notes.title: Measurements of an Empty Mound
notes.author: Ulvo Nerano
pages: The mound east of Kagrumez is open from within; the earth is thrown outward, not dug inward. Depth of the hollow: nine paces. Length: twenty-two. No bones. Scorching on the north lip, consistent with dragon fire. I have consulted the Skaal, who were unhelpful, and the master, who was less helpful still and asked whether I had finished my work at Kagrumez yet. I had not. I went back to Kagrumez. One does not argue with an empty grave of that size.
